final_candidates.decision_summary: Trp17 is a verified bulky aromatic residue in the N-terminal hydrophobic/aromatic segment. Substitution with glutamate removes favorable packing potential and introduces a potentially unfavorable charge.
Ile33 is a verified residue in the central Ile-Ile-Tyr-Pro-Val-Ile-Val cluster. Glutamate introduction is expected to disrupt hydrophobic packing if this segment contributes to the folded core.

Val38 is a verified hydrophobic residue near the end of the central hydrophobic cluster. Replacing it with glutamate is a strong local destabilization hypothesis while preserving a single-residue change.

stop_reason.detail: The current Top-3 are the most direct and internally consistent folding-disruption candidates available from sequence-only reasoning.

history.rationale: W17 is a bulky hydrophobic aromatic residue in the central conserved-looking region; replacing it with glutamate introduces charge and strongly disrupts hydrophobic packing.
Trp17 is a bulky hydrophobic aromatic residue; replacement with glutamate is expected to strongly disrupt local packing.
I33 lies within a hydrophobic stretch (I33-Y34-P35-V36-I37-V38); glutamate substitution should destabilize local core packing.
Ile33 lies in the central hydrophobic portion of the short protein, making charge introduction a plausible destabilizing change.
V38 is part of the same hydrophobic cluster and replacement by a charged glutamate is expected to be strongly folding-disruptive.
Val38 is within a hydrophobic cluster around positions 33-40, and glutamate should be poorly accommodated if this region forms a folded core.
Y16 precedes W17 and Y18 in an aromatic-rich segment; conversion to glutamate removes aromatic packing and introduces an unfavorable buried charge.
A Tyr-to-Glu replacement near Trp17 should disrupt aromatic and hydrophobic interactions.
Y34 is centrally located in a hydrophobic sequence segment; replacing it with glutamate should impair stabilizing packing interactions.
Tyr34-to-Glu combines aromatic-core removal with an unfavorable buried charge hypothesis.
I37 is a hydrophobic residue in the core-like I33-Y34-P35-V36-I37-V38 region; aspartate introduces charge and reduces hydrophobic stabilization.
Asp at a central isoleucine can destabilize a hydrophobic fold, though it is slightly less disruptive than glutamate candidates.
F40 is a bulky aromatic residue immediately following the hydrophobic cluster; glutamate substitution should disrupt local packing.
Phe40-to-Glu removes a bulky hydrophobic side chain and introduces charge in the central sequence segment.
V24 occurs in the V21-G22-T23-V24-A25 segment; a charged substitution may destabilize this structured hydrophobic region.
Val24-to-Glu is a plausible local destabilizer but is less clearly central than positions 33-40.
F48 is an aromatic residue in the latter half of the protein; glutamate substitution is likely to disrupt local hydrophobic interactions.
Phe48-to-Glu may impair packing, although the nearby glycine/serine-rich sequence could be more flexible or exposed.
L65 is near the C terminus and replacement with glutamate may destabilize the terminal region, although terminal residues may be less structurally critical.
Leu65 is near the C terminus and substitution with glutamate is less likely to globally disrupt folding than central hydrophobic-core candidates.

rejection.reason: Leu65 is near the C terminus and substitution with glutamate is less likely to globally disrupt folding than central hydrophobic-core candidates.

history.rationale: Ile32 is a verified central hydrophobic residue immediately adjacent to the I33/Y34/P35/V36/I37/V38 cluster; Glu introduction is a strong folding-disruption hypothesis.
